profile.reading:
Per QTS's own site, Ashburn 1 (DC1, operational) sits at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, VA 20166, part of a 28-acre campus with 55+ MW of critical power capacity in DC1; a second building (DC2, 22280 Randolph Drive) was under construction with 22.5+ MW planned to come online Q2 2026 and is not part of this specific registry entry. The site offers liquid cooling for high-density workloads and carries LEED and Energy Star certification. This is also the address QTS's own site lists as its US headquarters.

QTS Data Centers (shown on this row under its pre-2013-IPO name, "Quality Technology Services") was founded in 2003 in Overland Park, Kansas. Per Blackstone's own press release, Blackstone Real Estate Income Trust (BREIT) and other Blackstone-affiliated funds completed a roughly $10 billion acquisition of QTS Realty Trust on August 31, 2021, taking the company private at $78 per share; QTS is no longer an independent SEC filer. QTS's own site lists its US headquarters at 22271 Broderick Drive, Sterling, Virginia, placing this Northern Virginia "Data Center Alley" corridor, alongside neighboring hyperscale and colocation campuses from Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, at the center of the company's operations.

Dominion Energy, the dominant electric utility across Northern Virginia's data center corridor, has repeatedly cited data center demand growth as a primary driver of its long-term transmission and generation planning, and Loudoun and Prince William County officials have both cited data center real estate and business-license tax revenue as a significant share of their county budgets. QTS's Virginia campuses sit within this same regional grid and policy environment as neighboring hyperscale and colocation buildings operated by Amazon, Equinix, Digital Realty, and CyrusOne, all tracked elsewhere in this registry.

reading.body:
QTS Ashburn 1 holds 55 MW of IT critical power capacity in Sterling, Virginia, making it the fifth-largest published facility in a state where only 19 of 326 mapped facilities report a megawatt figure at all.

The 55 MW figure represents the operational DC1 building only. A second building under construction is expected to add 22.5 MW in the second quarter of 2026, meaning the published total will grow once that phase completes. At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this facility supports roughly 1,375 racks today. At colocation density of 10 kW per rack, it supports 5,500 racks. These are assumptions about how the power will be used, not operator specifications.

Virginia's concentration of data center capacity is real but largely unmeasured. Published capacity across all Virginia facilities sums to 1,326 MW, but this comes from only 19 of the 326 facilities in the registry. The true state total is unknown because most operators do not publish power figures. QTS Ashburn 1 ranks among the larger single-operator disclosures in Virginia, but it represents only 4 percent of the published state total and exists in a region where the actual power footprint is substantially larger than the data can show.

The facility holds LEED and Energy Star certifications, which address building efficiency and environmental design. No uptime tier, security attestation, or federal compliance designation is published, so none can be inferred from the available record.
